Nina (Customer): Hey team — since we flipped on function-calling + structured JSON outputs for our assistant, our p95/p99 latencies shot up. p95 went from ~140ms to ~920ms and p99 to ~2.4s. Happening across a handful of routes. Customer impact: slow front-end interactions, some timeouts.

Nina (Customer): Repro steps:
1) curl POST to https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat with header X-Feature:func-calls
2) body includes 'functions' array + 'response_schema' JSON schema
3) request_id: req-2026-03-15-88a2

Example request (redacted):
```
POST /v1/chat
Authorization: Bearer <key>
Content-Type: application/json
X-Feature: func-calls
{
  "model": "rw-tool-lite-v1",
  "messages": [{"role":"user","content":"get latest order status for 12345"}],
  "functions": [{"name":"order.lookup","parameters":{ "type":"object","properties":{"order_id":{"type":"string"}},"required":["order_id"]}}],
  "response_schema": {"type":"object","properties":{"order_id":{"type":"string"},"status":{"type":"string"}},"required":["order_id","status"]}
}
```

Nina (Customer): We can reproduce reliably in eu-west-1. Attaching trace id span: trace-0a1b2c.

Lina (Support): Thanks @Nina — filing escalation. Can you confirm which SDK / raw curl and your model variant? Also last_message_ts for the failed request would help. Tagging runtime + SRE. @Jamal @Sam

Lina (Support): Any quick mitigation we can try to reduce p95 while we investigate?

Jamal (Runtime Eng): Thanks — I pulled the trace (trace-0a1b2c). Router shows a long synchronous span `tool_router.dispatch` taking ~680ms in many samples. The model generation spans are fine. Looks like the overhead is between model output -> function routing -> schema validation -> final mux.

Jamal (Runtime Eng): Quick trace query we ran in APM:
```
service:runtime and span:tool_router.dispatch and trace.id:trace-0a1b2c
```

Sam (SRE): Correlating metrics: after the tools/structured-output rollout (2026-03-14 17:30 UTC) p95 jumped from ~140ms to 880-950ms; p99 up to 2.4s. CPU on router pods spiked; threadpool queue length for validator workers increased. Dashboard: https://observability.redwood/boards/latency/regressions (link) :warning:

Sam (SRE): Logs snippet from router pod (req-2026-03-15-88a2):
```
[2026-03-15T18:04:02Z] req=req-2026-03-15-88a2 span=tool_router.dispatch duration=672ms details="running schema validation"
[2026-03-15T18:04:02Z] req=req-2026-03-15-88a2 span=tool_call.execute duration=45ms details="call OK"
```

Jamal (Runtime Eng): Root cause hypothesis: current implementation runs full AJV JSON Schema validation in-process synchronously for every tool/structured output, and it happens before we return the stream chunk to the client. For complex schemas or nested objects this can be costly, and it's executed per-candidate route trying to pick the best tool. Also router currently tries tools sequentially for compatibility checks which multiplies the work.

Priya (Eng-ML): Also seeing extra tokenization overhead: function-calling metadata and structured output annotations increase token count slightly which causes small extra generation time and more KV cache pressure. But majority of this regression is CPU-bound validation and router sequencing.

Jamal (Runtime Eng): Immediate mitigations we can offer customers: 
1) Header based opt-out for in-process schema validation: `X-Redwood-Skip-Schema-Validate: true` — this will skip AJV validation and return the generated JSON as-is (we still run lightweight parse sanity checks).
2) Route requests to the 'rw-tool-lite-v1' tuned runtime which has async validator workers and higher router concurrency.
3) For customers who can tolerate eventual validation, enable `X-Redwood-Async-Validate: true` which accepts response and kicks off background validation + audit logs; if validation fails we emit a follow-up event but client latency isn't affected.

Jamal (Runtime Eng): Quick curl to try opt-out:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'X-Redwood-Skip-Schema-Validate: true' \
  -d @payload.json
```

Lina (Support): @Nina — can you try the skip header for a couple of requests and tell us p95/p99? If that helps we’ll propose it as a short-term workaround while eng works the fix.

Nina (Customer): Tried it. p95 dropped from ~920ms to ~160ms, p99 ~270ms for the same request set. Huge improvement. No functional regressions yet in our tests — we're validating payloads client-side too.

Nina (Customer): Confirming we can use this as a temporary workaround. Please let me know ETA for a proper fix — we need it globally not just eu-west-1.

Sam (SRE): Long-term work items (tracked):
- Move AJV validation off the hot request path into a fast worker pool (JIRA RW-TOOLS-412).
- Parallelize tool compatibility checks and short-circuit on positive match (RW-TOOLS-413).
- Add per-tool LRU cache for schema validation results keyed by schema hash + shape fingerprint (RW-TOOLS-414).
- Add telemetry to break down router time into `parse`, `validate`, `dispatch` spans.

Priya (Eng-ML): Also adding an ML-side optimization: tune tokenization to avoid repeated re-tokenization of function metadata by caching tokenized templates per-model. Added RW-OPT-205.

Jamal (Runtime Eng): Rollout plan: hotfix to expose `X-Redwood-Skip-Schema-Validate` and `X-Redwood-Async-Validate` flags to Console and SDKs within 24 hours (canary 4 pods in eu-west-1), medium-term (2 weeks) deploy worker-pool async validator and router parallelization, longer-term (1-2 months) deeper router refactor + schema result caching.

Lina (Support): I've documented the temp workaround and communicated to the customer. Creating follow-up ticket and assigned to Jamal for the hotfix, Sam for SRE rollout ops.

deploy-bot: Deployed canary: rw-router v1.9.3-canary to cluster eu-west-1 at 2026-03-15T20:10:00Z :rocket:

Jamal (Runtime Eng): Canary logs look good; p95 on canary dropped ~600ms versus pre-hotfix. Will monitor for errors.

Nina (Customer): Appreciate the quick help — will keep testing and report anomalies.

Lina (Support): Closing thread for now — follow-ups in RW-TOOLS-412/413/414 and RW-OPT-205. Will re-open if customer reports issues after canary. Thanks team :thumbsup:
